描述_ZN: The Book of Stories of People, Ming, Qiu Ying, silk, color, 41.4 cm in length and 33.8 cm in width per opening.　　The book has ten openings, the contents of which are drawn from historical stories, fables and legends, anecdotes of literati and poetic allegories, specifically, Zilu asks for the Jin, Ming Concubine Goes to the Cypress, Guifei Diao Makeup, South China Autumn Water, Blowing a Cock and Attracting a Phoenix, High Mountains and Flowing Water, Bamboo Courtyard Pin Gu, Pine Forest Six Escapees, Xunyang Pipa, Catching Willow Flowers, and so on. These subjects were often depicted by painters in history, but Qiu Ying injected his own talent and skills in the conception, image shaping and ink expression of his works, showing a distinctive individual style.　　The works are clearly themed and cleverly conceived, with not only specific and clear details of the characters' activities, but also attention to the setting and atmosphere, making each page highly ornamental. For example, the page of "Your Concubine's Makeup" is centered on Yang Guifei's early morning bun in the mirror at the Duanzheng Building of the Huaqing Palace, with the courtesans playing music, picking flowers and carrying a pipa in one scene, concentrating on her love of peonies, her love of hairpin flowers, her good music and her good dressing, and also reflecting her luxurious and happy life in general. Another example is the page of "High Mountain and Flowing Water", which is based on the story of Boya drumming his zither. While depicting the specific plot of Yu Boya playing his zither in a pavilion and Zhong Ziqi picking up the steps to meet his soulmate, the quiet and secluded environment of a high mountain waterfall and a pine forest with flowing water is set up to express the musical content of high mountain and flowing water imaginatively and to set off the elegant sentiments of the characters. It creates a perfect situation of intermingling scenes.　　This album uses the heavy-color brush method. The characters are delicately depicted, the literati are elegant and graceful, and the ladies are dignified and beautiful. The architectural vessels are neat and fine, and the mountains, rocks, and trees have their own forms. The brushwork is meticulous but not stagnant, smooth and natural, rigid and soft. The colors are brilliant and harmonious, and the overall tone is harmonious and elegant. The work has the artistic effect of elegance and vulgarity, and is Qiu Ying's innovation and development of the painting method of painting with heavy brush in the Tang and Song dynasties.
